newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Beijing-appointed assembly passes omnibus bill.
newsitem.headline: HK's Beijing-appointed assembly passes omnibus bill.

text.p: Hong Kong's new Beijing-appointed legislature quickly passed an omnibus bill on Tuesday activating laws it adopted ahead of the formal handover of this former British colony to Communist China.

The omnibus bill, adopted by a voice vote in the 60-member assembly just hours into the first day of Chinese rule, approved legislation including curbs on protests and the funding of political parties.
The nine-part bill also endorsed the appointments of top judges of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) and the establishment of its legal system.

The Beijing-appointed parliament was meeting in its first session on Hong Kong soil. Pro-democracy groups have strongly criticised the curbs on political reforms introduced near the end of British rule.
Rita Fan, the chamber's president, told legislators that in the next few months they should try to pass an electoral law so that elections could be held as soon as possible.
Hong Kong's new leader, Tung Chee-hwa, has pledged that the elections for a new legislature would be held next May.
